# Astrophysics and cosmology

<!-- Generated by scripts/build_prompts.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

Open only the cards whose "Applies when" line matches the paper. Paths are relative to this folder; the index of all folders is [../../INDEX.md](../../INDEX.md).

| Id | Card | Applies when |
|---|---|---|
| T-ASTEROSEISMOLOGY | [Asteroseismology and stellar parameters](asteroseismology.md) | the paper detects stellar oscillations or uses their frequencies to infer stellar properties, measures a large frequency separation, frequency of maximum power, period spacings or individual mode frequencies, or derives stellar masses, radii, ages or evolutionary states from asteroseismic scaling relations or seismic modelling |
| T-ASTRONOMICAL-SPECTROSCOPY | [Astronomical spectroscopy and redshifts](astronomical-spectroscopy.md) | the paper measures redshifts, velocities, line identifications or line fluxes from ultraviolet, optical or infrared spectra of galaxies, quasars, stars or transients, or claims spectroscopic confirmation of a high-redshift or photometrically selected candidate; precise stellar radial velocities and exoplanet spectra have their own cards |
| T-ASTROPHYSICAL-TRANSIENTS | [Astrophysical transients](astrophysical-transients.md) | the paper detects, localises or classifies a transient such as a fast radio burst, gamma-ray burst, supernova or tidal disruption event, associates it with a host galaxy or with a detection by another instrument or messenger, or infers transient rates or populations |
| CL-INDIRECT-DARK-MATTER | [Claims of indirect dark matter signals](indirect-dark-matter.md) | the paper reports an excess of gamma rays or X-rays, a spectral line, or an excess of cosmic-ray positrons, antiprotons or antinuclei over the expected astrophysical emission, and attributes it to the annihilation or decay of dark matter |
| CL-MOLECULAR-DETECTIONS | [Claims of molecular detections in space and planetary atmospheres](molecular-detections.md) | the paper claims that a molecule is detected, tentatively detected or newly identified in an interstellar, circumstellar, cometary, planetary or exoplanet spectrum, or bases such a claim on line assignments, stacked or cross-correlated lines, or comparison of models with and without the molecule |
| CL-MULTI-MESSENGER | [Claims of multi-messenger associations](multi-messenger.md) | the paper claims that signals from different messengers or instruments share a source, identifies a counterpart or host for a neutrino, gravitational-wave or cosmic-ray signal, or reports such a signal's coincidence in time or direction with a catalogue, alert or transient |
| T-CMB-MEASUREMENTS | [Cosmic microwave background measurements](cmb-measurements.md) | the paper measures cosmic microwave background temperature or polarization maps or power spectra, separates Galactic foregrounds from them, or bases a claim about B-mode polarization, the tensor-to-scalar ratio, cosmic birefringence or polarized foregrounds on such data |
| T-DISTANCE-LADDER | [Distance ladder and the Hubble constant](distance-ladder.md) | the paper measures galaxy distances with Cepheids, the tip of the red giant branch or other stellar standard candles, calibrates Type Ia supernovae or another secondary indicator, derives the Hubble constant, or claims agreement or tension between Hubble constant measurements |
| T-EXOPLANET-ATMOSPHERES | [Exoplanet atmospheres](exoplanet-atmospheres.md) | the paper reports a transmission, emission or high-resolution cross-correlation spectrum of an exoplanet, or bases a claim about atmospheric composition, a molecular detection, abundances, metallicity, clouds or temperature structure on such spectra or on an atmospheric retrieval |
| T-RADIAL-VELOCITIES | [Exoplanet radial velocities](radial-velocities.md) | the paper measures stellar radial velocities with a spectrograph, analyses a radial-velocity time series with periodograms or Keplerian fits, or bases a claim of a planet, its period, eccentricity, minimum mass or mass on Doppler data |
| T-EXOPLANET-TRANSITS | [Exoplanet transits](exoplanet-transits.md) | the paper reports a planet or planet candidate found by transit photometry, validates or confirms a transiting planet, or bases a claim about planet radius, orbit, eccentricity, occurrence rate or false-positive probability on transit light curves |
| T-GALAXY-SURVEYS | [Galaxy surveys and large-scale structure](galaxy-surveys.md) | the paper measures galaxy or quasar clustering from a survey catalogue, such as correlation functions, power spectra, baryon acoustic oscillations, redshift-space distortions or angular clustering, or bases a cosmological constraint on such statistics, photometric redshift distributions or covariances from mock catalogues |
| T-GRAVITATIONAL-LENSING | [Gravitational lensing](gravitational-lensing.md) | the paper measures weak-lensing shear, cosmic shear or galaxy-galaxy or cluster lensing, models a strongly lensed system, infers masses, magnifications, time delays, the Hubble constant or dark matter substructure from lensing, or interprets a microlensing event |
| T-GRAVITATIONAL-WAVES | [Gravitational-wave detection](gravitational-waves.md) | the paper reports or analyses gravitational-wave candidates from laser interferometer data, quotes a false-alarm rate or probability of astrophysical origin, or bases a claim about source masses, spins, distance, sky position, populations or tests of gravity on such signals |
| T-HIGH-CONTRAST-IMAGING | [High-contrast and direct imaging](high-contrast-imaging.md) | the paper detects, characterises or rules out faint companions, planets or circumstellar disc structure near a bright star using coronagraphy, adaptive optics or point-spread-function subtraction, or reports contrast curves, companion astrometry or model-based companion masses from such images |
| T-PHOTOMETRY | [Photometry and light curves](photometry.md) | the paper measures the brightness of astronomical sources in images, builds light curves by aperture, point-spread-function or differential photometry, or bases a claim about magnitudes, fluxes, colours, variability, periods, transits, eclipses or event timing on them |
| T-RADIO-INTERFEROMETRY | [Radio astronomy and interferometry](radio-interferometry.md) | the paper reports images, flux densities, spectra or detections from a radio or millimetre interferometer (aperture-synthesis array), or bases a claim about compact or extended structure, a spectral line, a faint source or a non-detection on interferometric visibilities or images |
| T-SUPERNOVA-COSMOLOGY | [Supernova cosmology](supernova-cosmology.md) | the paper uses type Ia supernovae as distance indicators, fits or standardises their light curves, builds or analyses a supernova Hubble diagram, or bases a claim about distances, the expansion history, dark energy or the Hubble constant on supernova brightnesses |
| T-HIGH-ENERGY-ASTRONOMY | [X-ray and gamma-ray astronomy](high-energy-astronomy.md) | the paper analyses photon-counting data from an X-ray or gamma-ray telescope, or a ground-based Cherenkov telescope, and bases a claim on a source detection, flux, spectrum, spectral line, extension or upper limit derived from event counts and instrument responses |
